chapter: Chicago memories and the road to the Navy
title: Tony Jackson and the piano players of New Orleans' 25 club
summary: He went to Chicago wanting to hear Tony Jackson, whose fame he knew from the '25' where New Orleans piano players and pimps hung out. Marge never heard Jackson.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: But what I wanted to hear was Tony Jackson.

Yes. Oh, I'd heard of him from New Orleans because that's all you could hear. You see the crowd where I hung out, you see I lived way up town. I used to, Steve Lewis used to bring me down to '25.' That was a place where piano players in the afternoon would hang out. And all of them were sharp and pimp style, you know.

And I'd go down there, and oh, I, all I could hear was Tony Jackson and Louis Wade and (Clark) Wade was his brother, who was a big time pimp. And another cat, Bob Row, he was a hell of a piano player.
Well, these guys were both pimps and piano players?
That's what where Jelly Roll was a pimp.
Yes, Jelly Roll was a pimp.
Well wasn't Tony Jackson from St. Louis originally?
No, he was from New Orleans?

He was a New Orleans boy. I think he was from New Orleans. And then we had another lovely cat around New Orleans who was a great violinist. Andrew Roseman. He had been to the conservatory; boy, but he was a hell of a violinist.
Well I mean, would he be playing sort of jazz or would he be playing ......
I've got to go peat again, folks.
Well what sort of piano player
Was he like Jelly Roll or?
I don't know. I don't know a thing about Tony Jackson.
Zutty, you know, started telling me about it. I know Jelly Roll. I heard Jelly Roll all the time.
